{narrating} With Cooke dead, the Powder Gangers at Vault 19 fell apart.
{narrating} Those who weren't destroyed by the Courier fled into the hills or attempted to work their way back through the Mojave Wasteland. Few survived.
{narrating} Armed with a wide array of improvised explosives and stolen weapons, the Vault 19 Powder Gang tormented the Mojave Wasteland for years.
{narrating} Citizens of the NCR were favorite targets, and they always suffered the worst fates.
{narrating} After the Vault 19 Powder Gang surrendered to the NCR, they were re-incorporated into the correctional system.
{narrating} The NCR did increase their sentences, as they aren't about to take off time for good behavior.
{narrating} After the majority of the Vault 19 Powder Gangers joined the Great Khans, the weaker members scattered throughout the Mojave Wasteland.
{narrating} Though a few managed to erase their pasts, most never survived the journey.

topics.prompt: I took care of those geckos.

responses.text: What do you want to know?
There are some fire geckos in the lower levels of the Vault. We need to get them gone so we can get to the sulfur.
You go clear them out for us, and there'll be some caps for you.
I want you to head to Red Rock Canyon, north of here. Find Papa Khan and ask him if he'd allow the Powder gangers to join up.
Bye.

topics.prompt: Do you know anything about this vault?

responses.text: You really don't know? I'm Samuel Cooke. I was the brains behind the NCRCF prison break.
Their "republic" is a joke. They're a bunch of tyrants led by an even greater tyrant, that idiot Kimball.
They think they have the right to annex every inch of dirt in the West and force their system on every man, woman, and child.
He was an inmate like the rest of us. He had his uses, but he's a coward and a troublemaker.
He was an inmate like the rest of us. He was useful during the jailbreak, but now...

I was blowing up supply caravans along the 15 freeway. The NCR got wise to my ambush spots, picked me up and threw me in a cage.

topics.prompt: How did you end up in prison?

responses.text: A beautiful thing. Saved a little blast powder here, hid a makeshift weapon there, and one day I orchestrated a little symphony for the NCR.

topics.prompt: Tell me about the prison break.

responses.text: Didn't have a choice. He was confusing the men, and I need to control them or we're just a bunch of disorganized idiots.

topics.prompt: What do you want the sulfur for?

responses.text: There aren't enough of us here to make a real impact on the NCR, and the Khans probably hate the NCR more than we do. Strength in numbers, they say.
So, will you talk to Papa Khan on our behalf?

topics.prompt: Why do you want to join the Great Khans?

responses.text: Great. Come back as soon as you can.
Great. Get to it. Oh, and take this - there's some weird shit with this Vault's security and some doors will only open if you have a keycard.

topics.prompt: So, what brought you to this place?

responses.text: It's a fucking deathtrap around here. Fiends swarm all over Vault 3 in the east, and there are fucking Deathclaws south of that, at Quarry Junction.
If you're looking for humans, the Khans are north of us and an NCR base at McCarran, past Vault 3. Supposedly there are muties to the southeast.

topics.prompt: Tell me about the area outside the vault.

responses.text: Like raiders, but worse - these guys are messed up on every damn chem there is. You can spot them by the horned skulls they wear as hats.

topics.prompt: Tell me about the Great Khans.

responses.text: I've heard the muties there are different. Completely insane, and supposedly they use some kind of invisibility technology. I'd stay away.

topics.prompt: Tell me about the super mutants.

responses.text: Good. Hey, I got another job for you if you're interested.
